name: Amazon Aurora
tagline: AWS's MySQL- and PostgreSQL-compatible engine on a shared, six-way replicated storage layer.
description: Aurora is AWS's re-engineered MySQL- and PostgreSQL-compatible relational service. It keeps the familiar engines' query layers but replaces their storage with a log-structured volume replicated six ways across three Availability Zones, which gives fast crash recovery, up to 15 low-lag read replicas sharing the same storage, and copy-on-write clones. Aurora Serverless v2 scales capacity in fine-grained ACUs and can now pause to zero, while Global Database replicates to other regions for DR and local reads. It is the default choice for AWS shops that want managed MySQL or Postgres with better availability than RDS, at the cost of AWS lock-in and I/O-sensitive pricing.

pricing.notes: Pay per instance-hour or Serverless v2 ACU-hour plus storage; Aurora Standard bills I/O, Aurora I/O-Optimized bundles it. New AWS accounts get Free Tier credits rather than a dedicated Aurora free tier.

scale.notes: Single writer per cluster with up to 15 read replicas; storage grows automatically to 128 TiB-class volumes; Aurora PostgreSQL Limitless Database adds managed sharding.

strengths: Six-way replicated storage across three AZs with fast failover (typically under 30 s)
Up to 15 read replicas sharing one storage volume with millisecond-level lag
Copy-on-write fast clones for test environments and analytics snapshots
Serverless v2 scales in half-ACU steps and can pause to zero capacity
Global Database for cross-region DR and local reads
Zero-ETL integrations into Redshift and other AWS analytics services
weaknesses: AWS-only; storage layer and features are not portable
Single writer per cluster limits write scaling without Limitless
Costs can spike with I/O-heavy workloads on the Standard configuration
Engine versions and extensions lag upstream MySQL/PostgreSQL releases
useCases: Production MySQL or PostgreSQL backends on AWS
Spiky or dev/test workloads on Serverless v2
Cross-region disaster recovery with Global Database
pgvector-based semantic search next to relational data
notIdealFor: Write-heavy workloads exceeding one large writer
